targets.authors: Lowry, P. B., Moody, G. D., Gaskin, J., Galletta, D. F., Humpherys, S.L., Barlow, J. B., & Wilson, D. W.
targets.title: Evaluating journal quality and the Association for Information Systems senior scholars’ journal basket via bibliometric measures: Do expert journal assessments add value?
targets.evidence_quote: We replicated their study using the same sample of 21 journals, and as well as with a larger sample of 73 journals.
targets.outcome_quote: Based on the narrow sample replication, our rank ordering is the same for the top three of MISQ, ISR, and JMIS. The broader sample replication also ranks MISQ first and JMIS third, but ISR fourth, not second, and JAIS is second. Both replication approaches rank ISJ eighth, whereas it ranks fifth in Lowry et al. Our analysis, as noted above, does not support the claims of excessive self-citation in JIT.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Across the close and expanded-sample attempts the authors report support for several original rankings and basket-versus-comparison differences, but explicitly contradict the original claim about JIT self-citation and some rankings. Agreement with the broad purpose in the abstract is not an overall replication verdict. Appendix A9 states both agreement and disagreement in four consecutive sentences.

targets.authors: Dean, D. L., Lowry, P. B., & Humpherys, S.
targets.title: Profiling the research productivity of tenured Information Systems faculty at U.S. institutions.
targets.evidence_quote: Following their procedures, we limited our sample to recent cases of designated IS scholars in U.S. business schools, but used a more recent time frame, and found very similar results. Details of our modest replication of their study are found in the Appendix (Table A1).
targets.outcome_quote: Our results are very close to those in Dean et al. (2011). They found that promoted IS scholars published 23% of their articles in CS and Engineering journals; we find 24%. They found 22% of articles in non-IS business journals; we find 21%.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The appendix explicitly reports a separate replication in a new sample of promoted faculty and compares the original publication proportions with almost identical new proportions.

reasoning: Complete 41-page article with references and appendix; title, DOI and both authors match. Includes two original papers: focal Lowry journal-ranking paper and independently replicated Dean faculty-publication paper in Appendix A1. Code as replication because the work uses an expanded journal sample and independently gathered bibliometric data, including later Google Scholar citations, and a new faculty sample. Some reconstruction of original matrices informs methods, but the central tests use newly acquired or expanded observations. Neither original DOI is printed in its reference entry.
